fieldMarks: Heavy-bodied tree squirrel, 19-29 in and 1-3 lb, larger than the gray squirrel.
Back and sides reddish yellow mixed with gray; belly and tail fringe reddish yellow to orange.
Black individuals occur, notably in some southeastern populations.
Ear tufts often develop in winter.
behavior: Active by day and mostly in trees; generally solitary except during mating chases.
Barks and chatters; threatens with an upright stance and tail flicks.
Prefers acorns, hickory nuts, walnuts, mulberry and hawthorn seeds, and scatter-caches nuts for winter.
Nests in tree cavities or bulky leaf nests averaging about 40 ft up.
habitat: Deciduous and mixed forest with varied mast trees, often on ridges, farm woodlots, timbered fence rows and hedgerows in prairie country, and towns with large oaks and hickories.
range: Eastern and central United States, north into Canada and south into northern Mexico; introduced into urban areas of western North America.

lookalikes.name: Eastern gray squirrel
lookalikes.howToTell: Gray squirrel is slimmer and smaller with a gray back and white belly and tail fringe.
